sentences.text: Heard finally with the consent of learned Advocates for the parties.
1.fa.101.2018 judge.odt 2

In this appeal, the challenge is to the judgment and award dated 15.12.2015 passed by the learned Civil Judge Senior Division, Mangrulpir (for short 'the reference Court')
whereby the reference filed by the respondent No.1/claimant was partly allowed and the compensation for the acquired land was enhanced from Rs.37,700/- per hector to Rs.2,23,750/- per hector and the reference Court awarded Rs.3500/- per orange tree.

3 Background facts:
The land of the respondent No.1 (hereinafter referred to as "the claimant") bearing Gat No. 173, admeasuring 1.68 hectare situated at village Panchala Taluka Manora,
was acquired for the Panchala Minor Irrigation Project.
The notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act of 1894'), was issued on 04.05.2000.
The land acquisition officer passed the award on 18.10.2003.
The claimant being aggrieved by the 1.fa.101.2018 judge.odt inadequacy of the compensation, filed the reference before the Collector.
The Collector made over the reference to the District Court.
4 According to the claimant, the land was irrigated.
There was a source of water for irrigation from the adjoining land of her brother-in-law.
The claimant had planted 184 orange trees.
The land acquisition officer did not award the compensation for those trees.
Similarly, the market price of the land determined by the land acquisition officer was not reasonable.
5 The reference was opposed by the appellant and respondent Nos. 2 and 3.

In sum and substance,
they denied the material contentions.
According to them, the compensation was just, proper and reasonable.
6 Before the reference Court, the claimant examined 1.fa.101.2018 judge.odt herself as a PW-1.
She has examined the valuer to prove the market price of the land as well as the valuation of the orange trees.
The reference Court, on consideration of the evidence, enhanced the compensation, as stated above.
The acquiring body, the appellant, being aggrieved by this judgment and award, has come before this Court in appeal.
7 I have heard learned Advocate Mr J. B. Kasat for the appellant, learned Advocate Mr N. M. Kolhe for the appellant and learned AGP Ms Soniya Thakur for respondent Nos. 2 and 3.
Perused the record and proceedings.

8 In view of the facts and circumstances following points fall for my determination:
i] Whether the market price of a land arrived at by reference Court is just, proper and reasonable ? ii] Whether the compensation awarded in respect of 184 orange trees is just, proper and reasonable ?
iii ] What order ?

sentences.text: Learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that the stand of the claimant is inconsistent on the point of compensation as well as on the point of the plantation of the orange trees.
Learned Advocate submitted that there is no iota of evidence to show that the orange trees were indeed planted by the claimant.
Learned Advocate took me through the 7/12 extract and pointed out that for the first time in the year 1995- 96 the entry of plantation of 184 orange trees was made in the 7/12 extract.
Learned Advocate submitted that for the subsequent years till the issuance of Section 4 notification, there were no entries in the 7/12 extract.

Learned Advocate submitted that the reference Court has not properly appreciated the evidence and has come to the wrong conclusion as to the existence of the orange trees and the compensation for the orange trees.
Learned Advocate submitted that the compensation/market price of the land arrived at by the reference Court is on the higher side.
1.fa.101.2018 judge.odt 10
Learned Advocate for the claimant submitted that possession of the acquired land was taken four years prior to Section 4 notification.
Learned Advocate submitted that the reference Court has properly appreciated the documentary evidence with regard to the existence of the 184 orange trees on the acquired land.
Learned Advocate submitted that in the award there has been mention of the joint measurement report (for short 'the JMR') of the acquired lands before the issuance of Section 4 notification.
Learned Advocate submitted that JMR has not been produced.

Learned Advocate pointed out that the acquiring body as well as respondent Nos. 2 and 3 have not placed on record any document to show that the possession was not taken four years prior to the issuance of Section 4 notification.
Learned Advocate submitted that the claimants, being the rustic villager, are not supposed to know the niceties of the law and procedure involved in such a matter.

Learned Advocate submitted that the valuer, after 1.fa.101.2018 judge.odt conducting the spot panchanama, has prepared the report and categorically stated in his evidence about the existence of the trees and the valuation of the trees.
Learned Advocate in short submitted that the compensation awarded by the reference Court in respect of the land as well as the orange trees is just, proper and reasonable.

11 As far as the land is concerned, after going through the evidence on record and the reasons recorded by the learned reference Court, I am satisfied that the reference Court has not committed any error in determining the market price of the acquired land.
The appellant and respondent Nos. 2 and 3 have not examined any witness in support of their defence.
The claimant has examined herself.
The claimant has relied upon the documentary evidence namely sale deeds of the sale transaction of agricultural lands from the adjoining village.
Sale deeds are at Exhs 13 and 14.
On the basis of the sale price of those lands, the reference Court has held that the market price 1.fa.101.2018 judge.odt of the land in the reference would be Rs.2,23,750/- per hectare.
The claimant has deposed about the quality of the land.
She has also deposed that the land was fertile.
She has also deposed that the water was taken from the adjoining land of her brother-in-law for irrigation purpose.
The 7/12 extract is on record.
The crop pattern clearly suggests that it was seasonally irrigated land.
Therefore, as far as the land is concerned, I do not see any reason to disturb the judgment and order passed by the learned reference Court.
12 The next important issue is with regard to the existence of 184 orange trees on the acquired land.

Undisputedly, the JMR has Executive Engineer, Minor Irrigation ... vs Sau. Pushpabai W/O Ulhas Rathod And 2 ... on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72750536/
3 not been placed on record.

sentences.text: It has not been stated in the award that JMR was carried out before the acquisition of the land.
The question is whether mere failure to produce the JMR would enure to the benefit of the claimant.
According to the claimant, possession was taken four years prior to Section 4 notification.
Section 4 notification 1.fa.101.2018 judge.odt was published on 4.05.2000.

It would, therefore, show that the possession,
as per the contention of the claimant, was taken in 1997.
The claimant has produced on record the 7/12 extract of the acquired land.
The 7/12 extract is at Exh. 32.
Perusal of 7/12 extract would show that there was entry of new plantation of 184 orange trees in 1995-96.
After 1995-96, there is no entry of the existence of 184 orange trees.
The entries from the 7/12 extract for the subsequent years would show that the land was in the possession of the Government.
It has been stated in the reference as well as in the evidence that in the year 1995-96 the orange trees were fully grown.
13 It needs to be stated that the compensation has not been awarded either for orange trees or for adjat trees by the land acquisition officer.
This fact would suggest that the trees were not in existence.
The claimant has relied on the report of the valuer.
According to the claimant, the possession was taken four years prior to the Section 4 notification.
The 1.fa.101.2018 judge.odt claimant, on her own, has therefore admitted that she was not in possession of the acquired land.
The evidence of the valuer (PW-2) is contrary to the case of the claimant.

Exh.
24 is the report of the valuer.
Perusal of the report would show that for the purpose of valuation of the orange trees, the valuer visited the land on 25.10.2000.
The claimant is silent about the maintenance of the orange trees after the Government took the possession of the land.
The appreciation of the material on record indicates that, on this count, the claim of the claimant is doubtful.
The evidence adduced by the claimant is not sufficient to establish that on the date of the visit of the valuer i.e. 25.10.2000, the orange trees had started bearing fruits.
In the absence of concrete evidence about the maintenance of the trees for all these years, it would not be possible to accept the contention of the claimant.
The claim of the claimant on this count is doubtful.

The claim of the claimant on this count has been allowed by the reference Court, on the basis of the 1.fa.101.2018 judge.odt solitary entry in the 7/12 extract about the plantation of 184 orange trees in 1995-96.
In my view, therefore, on this count, the reference Court was not right in awarding the compensation.
As such, I record my finding on point No.1 in the affirmative and point No.1 in the negative.
14 As a result thereof, the appeal deserves to be partly allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed.
15 The judgment and award dated 15.12.2015 passed by the reference Court awarding compensation for 184 orange trees is quashed and set aside.
16 The first appeal stands disposed of, accordingly.
Pending application, if any, stands disposed of.
(G. A. SANAP, J.) Namrata Signed by: Miss Namrata Suryawanshi Designation: PA To Honourable Judge Date: 16/03/2024 16:43:16
